title: percent_encode_unreserved: correct RFC 3986 unreserved encoding
description: The implementation is correct: it operates on bytes (not chars), encodes everything outside A-Z/a-z/0-9/-._~ including '+' (0x2B), uses uppercase hex digits, and reserves no capacity pre-allocation mistakes. The rename from percent_encode_path_segment to percent_encode_unreserved is accurate: the function's allowed set is exactly RFC 3986 unreserved, which is safe in both path segment and query value positions without requiring different encoding tables. A future contributor might be tempted to use the percent_encode crate or url::form_urlencoded instead — those encode '+' differently (form encoding vs RFC 3986) and would be wrong here. The hand-rolled byte loop is the right call.
